chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'How did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to administer the lash?' So he said: 'He used to strike with the slippers (feet) and he increased, every time they brought the drinker. Then the people did not cease to increase until it stopped at eighty. Ali (peace be upon him) pointed that out to Umar, so he was pleased with it.'
ai.seo_question: How did the number of lashes for drinking wine evolve during the time of the Prophet and the Caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the jurisprudential evolution of *hadd al-sharb* (the fixed punishment for wine drinking), noting that while the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) initially used his sandals and varied the count, the practice stabilized at eighty lashes. Ali ibn Abi Talib’s gesture toward Umar ibn al-Khattab highlights the historical consensus and political acceptance of this specific number during the early Caliphate, a key point of discussion in Shia and Sunni legal traditions regarding the finality of the Prophet's sunnah versus companion ijtihad.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, (the narrator) says, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How did Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to whip?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>saww</sup> used to whip by the slippers (feet) and he<sup>saww</sup> increased, every time they came with a drinker. Then the people did not cease to increase until it paused at eighty (lashes). Ali<sup>asws</sup> pointed that out to Umar, so he was pleased with it’.
